requirements.requirement: /tmp mounted with noexec, nosuid, nodev enforced
requirements.summary: tmp.mount.d override.conf sets Options=mode=1777,strictatime,nosuid,nodev,noexec; systemctl enable --now tmp.mount applied live. findmnt before reboot and after reboot both show /tmp as rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,seclabel. Functional proof: a chmod +x script placed in /tmp fails to execute (Permission denied, rc=126) both before and after reboot; a setuid-root file retains the SUID bit in stat output but the mount enforces nosuid; mknod-created device nodes in /tmp fail to open (Permission denied), demonstrating nodev.

requirements.requirement: /dev/shm mounted with noexec, nosuid, nodev enforced
requirements.summary: Baseline /dev/shm had only nosuid,nodev (no noexec). /etc/fstab updated with 'tmpfs /dev/shm tmpfs defaults,nosuid,nodev,noexec,seclabel 0 0' and the mount remounted live. findmnt before and after reboot shows rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,seclabel on /dev/shm. Functional proof: an executable copied into /dev/shm fails to run (Permission denied, rc=126) pre- and post-reboot; a mknod device node in /dev/shm fails to open for read/write (Permission denied), confirming nodev.

Pre-restart boot_id (bf4e9cbb...) and healthy mount state captured, reboot issued and acknowledged, polling confirmed a different post-restart boot_id (d431d1d5...) proving an actual restart occurred, and post-restart findmnt plus repeated exec/setuid functional tests confirm both /tmp and /dev/shm retained nosuid,nodev,noexec with tmp.mount enabled+active. This is independently corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, whose before/after boot-identity observations show the same boot_id transition (bf4e9cbb...→d431d1d5...).

overall_summary: The executor hardened both /tmp (via a systemd tmp.mount.d drop-in) and /dev/shm (via an /etc/fstab entry) with nosuid,nodev,noexec, verified the options live, functionally proved exec/setuid/device-node restrictions with concrete permission-denied results, and demonstrated persistence across an actual reboot (boot_id changed, independently corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshot's boot-identity observations). All three material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence. The only blemish is a small, low-risk leftover /etc/fstab backup file from the edit step.
limitations: The setuid functional proof conflates nosuid and noexec: since noexec already blocks all execution on both mounts, the evidence shows the SUID bit is retained in file metadata but does not independently isolate nosuid's effect from noexec's effect. This does not undermine the mount-option outcome (both options are confirmed present via findmnt) but slightly weakens the standalone functional demonstration of nosuid specifically.
No cleanup of the /etc/fstab.bak.* backup file was observed in the captured command timeline; it may still exist on node1.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command timeline reviewed chronologically. All state-changing commands map to a clear purpose: applying the fstab/tmp.mount.d hardening, live remount/enable, and bounded functional test files/device nodes that were created and then removed (exectest.sh, shmtest, setuidtest, devtest nodes) both before and after reboot, plus a deliberate reboot for the persistence proof. One minor residue: cmd-9047ad5ae8c84547 created a timestamped backup of /etc/fstab (/etc/fstab.bak.<timestamp>) before editing it, and no subsequent command shows it being removed — a low-risk, non-sensitive leftover file consistent with a reasonable backup-before-edit practice, but technically unnecessary residue that was not cleaned up. No failed/conflicting services, no unsafe exposure, and package-health/listening-sockets are unchanged apart from expected reboot-driven PID changes per the lifecycle comparison.
